title: Write It Do It B 2027
summary: Write It Do It has no written exam and no past paper anywhere — what tournaments publish is a materials list and a scoring rubric. One student writes a description of an object in twenty-five minutes; the other builds it from those words in twenty. The rubric awards points per piece for presence, size, colour, location, orientation and connection, and this course is built from those six words.
objectives: Write a description that fixes presence, size, colour, location, orientation and connection for every piece
Establish a reference frame and naming scheme before describing anything, and keep both consistent
Write unambiguous imperative steps in an order a builder can actually follow
Stay inside the no-drawings rule while using numerals, letters, abbreviations and symbols freely
Build from someone else's description, including deciding what to do with a step that is unclear

units.title: What the Rubric Actually Scores
units.summary: Points are awarded per piece for presence, size, colour, location, orientation and connection. Everything in this course serves those six words.
objectives: Name the six scored attributes and write for each
Know the two ways to be disqualified or tiered

lessons.title: Size, Colour, Location, Orientation, Connection
lessons.objective: List the five properties the rules score for each piece (proper size, color, location, orientation and connection), note that a piece must be placed to earn any of them, and write a sentence that fixes all five for one component.

lessons.title: No Drawings, and What Counts as One
lessons.objective: State what the rules forbid in a description, and what numerals, letters, abbreviations and symbols are still allowed.

lessons.title: Why One Wrong Connection Does Not End the Score
lessons.objective: Explain how pieces connected correctly beyond an incorrect connection still score, and what that means for describing order.

lessons.title: Writer and Doer
lessons.objective: State what each role may and may not do, including the rule about touching the object and the time split.

units.title: Saying Where Something Is
units.summary: Location and orientation are two of the six scored attributes, and they are where most points are lost.
objectives: Establish a reference frame before describing anything

lessons.title: Establishing a Frame Before You Start
lessons.objective: Set up a reference frame and orientation convention in the first sentences, so every later position is unambiguous.

lessons.title: Above, Below, Beside, Between
lessons.objective: Describe a piece's position relative to a previously described piece, using distances and directions rather than impressions.

lessons.title: Which Way It Points
lessons.objective: Describe orientation using angles, axes and named faces, and distinguish rotation from translation.

lessons.title: Sizes, Distances and Units
lessons.objective: Give dimensions and distances with units and a stated measuring convention, including how to describe size without a ruler.

lessons.title: Naming Pieces So They Stay Named
lessons.objective: Establish a naming scheme for the pieces at the start and use it consistently, including colour and count.

units.title: Writing It in Twenty-Five Minutes
units.summary: Technical writing under a clock, for a reader who cannot ask questions.
objectives: Order steps so the build can actually proceed

lessons.title: The Sentences That Get Built Wrong
lessons.objective: Identify ambiguous instructions and rewrite them, covering pronoun reference, 'it', 'the other one' and unstated assumptions.

lessons.title: Writing in the Imperative
lessons.objective: Write build steps as direct imperative instructions with one action per step.

lessons.title: An Order the Doer Can Follow
lessons.objective: Order steps so that every piece is attached to something already placed, and describe the base before what sits on it.

lessons.title: Starting With an Inventory
lessons.objective: Open the description with a full inventory of pieces by colour, count and size, and say why that costs less time than it saves.

lessons.title: Abbreviating Without Losing the Reader
lessons.objective: Use abbreviations and short identifiers consistently, given that the rules do not require defining them.

lessons.title: Reading It Back As the Doer
lessons.objective: Re-read a description from the builder's point of view and find the steps that cannot be executed as written.

units.title: Building From Someone Else's Words
units.summary: Twenty minutes, one description, no questions allowed.
objectives: Decide what to do when a step is unclear

lessons.title: Read It All Before You Touch Anything
lessons.objective: Read a whole description and lay out the inventory before building, and explain what that prevents.

lessons.title: When the Description Is Unclear
lessons.objective: Decide what to build when a step is ambiguous, choosing the reading that preserves the most later steps.

lessons.title: Twenty Minutes, and What Time Decides
lessons.objective: Use the 20-minute build well: read first, build in the description's order, place every piece you can, and know that construction time is used only as a tiebreaker.

lessons.title: The Shapes and Connections That Keep Appearing
lessons.objective: Recognise the common geometric arrangements and connection types used in these objects and the words that describe them.
